answer: Stop sybils with a violet seal, a hollow test, and a zephyr audit. Every identity carries a violet seal: a bond receipt chained to the last epoch's seal, so a fresh clone starts worthless and must age epochs to earn weight. A zephyr beacon picks identities each epoch for a memory-hard sequential proof salted by address; the work cannot be copied or parallelized. An identity failing the hollow test — no attestation edges, no seal history — is quarantined. The k-th seal one sponsor funds costs k squared, so N clones pay about N cubed, and one failed audit burns the whole seal chain.
